Find reference reaches that end outside their own divide

Source: R/check_reference_divide_pairing.R
check_reference_divide_pairing.Rd

A reach and its divide are a pair: the reach drains the divide, and its downstream end is the divide's outlet. Where the pair is wrong the two describe different places, and nothing downstream can reconcile them.

The splitter is where it shows. A parent divide is partitioned by seeding a masked D8 flood at each member's downstream endpoint, and the mask is the parent buffered by 250 m. An endpoint beyond that buffer has no grid cell to seed from, the partition is abandoned, and the whole parent passes to the downstream-most child while its siblings ship owning no land. Widening the mask is not the cure: it would let every parent's flood escape its own catchment.

Most endpoints sit marginally outside their divide because an outlet lies on the boundary, so the measure is distance rather than containment. Observed on the CONUS reference for VPU 04: of 150,744 paired reaches, 104,830 endpoints are within 30 m of their divide, and 147 (0.098%) are beyond 250 m, the worst 10.4 km away.

Report-only, and deliberately not wired into run_pipeline(). The pairing belongs to the reference and is not ours to change, and this asks a question about a reference release rather than about a VPU.

Usage

check_reference_divide_pairing(
  reference_gpkg,
  flowpath_layer = "flowpaths",
  divide_layer = "divides",
  id = "flowpath_id",
  vpuid = NA_character_,
  tolerance_m = 250,
  sample = NULL,
  strict = FALSE
)

Arguments

reference_gpkg

Path to the reference GeoPackage.

flowpath_layer, divide_layer

Layer names.

id

Identifier column, present in both layers.

vpuid

Optional VPU to restrict to, when the layers carry vpuid.

tolerance_m

Distance beyond which a pairing is reported. The default is the 250 m buffer the splitter masks with, so it is the distance at which the pairing stops being usable rather than merely imprecise.

sample

Number of pairs to test, or NULL for all.

strict

If TRUE, warn when any are found.

Value

Invisibly, a data frame of id, dist_m for the reaches found, furthest first.
